simple.meaning: לַעֲנָה (laʻănâh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “wormwood (regarded as poisonous, and therefore accursed).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 8 times across Deuteronomy, Proverbs, Jeremiah, Lamentations, Amos, beginning at Deuteronomy 29:17. Its contexts include birth, family, prophetic witness.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to לַעֲנָה (H3939).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: לַעֲנָה (laʻănâh) / H3939 is traced through Deuteronomy 29:17, Proverbs 5:4, Jeremiah 9:14, Jeremiah 23:15 as a generated source-based concept entry.

timeline.evidenceText: and you have seen their abominations and their idols of wood, stone, silver, and gold, which were among them);
but in the end she is as bitter as wormwood,
but have walked after the stubbornness of their own heart and after the Baals, which their fathers taught them.”
Therefore Yahweh of Armies says concerning the prophets:
He has filled me with bitterness.
Remember my affliction and my misery,

definitions.short: wormwood (regarded as poisonous, and therefore accursed)
definitions.full: H3939. laanah לַעֲנָה noun feminine wormwood (Late Hebrew id. ; Arabic is curse (verb id. ), so Nabataean לצנת (verb לען ) compare Cook Glossary ); — only figurative of bitter things: — of perverted justice, Amos 5:7 ; 6:12 (|| ראֹשׁ ; of result of idolatry, Deut 29:17 (|| id. ); of ׳י s chastisement Jer 9:14 (|| מֵ֯ירֿאֹשׁ , 23:15 (|| id. ), Lam 3:15 (|| מְרוֺרִים ), 3:19 (|| ראֹשׁ ); simile of bitter ( מָרָה ) result of intercourse with strange woman Prov 5:4 . — On wormwood (Artemisia absinthium , etc., Greek ἀψίθιον ) compare Löw 80f. 401, 421 Tristr Nat, Hist. Bib. 493 . לָעַע see לוע לפד (√ of following; meaning unknown).
